neighbours.label: qualifying an abstract ideal: 'X does not mean absolute X' and 'X is notoriously difficult to define' (equality, freedom, justice, normality); the + pole is the other side: concrete standards and limits being met or exceeded
fire: Liberty under the law does not mean absolute liberty to do as one pleases.
Equal opportunity does not imply strict equality of outcomes for everyone.
Notions like sanity and madness are notoriously difficult to define.
Neutrality in the classroom does not require total neutrality on every question.
Democracy is a slippery concept to define with any rigor.
Religious tolerance does not mean unlimited tolerance of every practice.
The idea of justice is not the same as perfect equality of treatment.
Terms such as art and beauty are notoriously hard to pin to a definition.
quiet: Walking along the shore does not take much time in the morning.
The new timetable does not include a late train for everyone.
Dishes like stew and soup are wonderfully easy to cook.
Parking near the classroom does not require a permit on weekends.
Cricket is a popular game to watch with any friend.
The radiation levels were higher than the legal limit in every sample.
The plant failed to meet stricter emission standards last year.
Shops such as bakers and butchers are usually open by seven.

notes: Weak-to-middling in probes: 'does not mean absolute equality' 0.57, 'difficult to define in practice' 0.38, six more of the same kind 0.22-0.28; 'said the risks outweigh', 'turn out to', 'concluded that' (all card top examples) only 0.03-0.07. So the label covers one strand of the card at about a quarter of max; a marginal median is likely.
